podcast.title: A record player for twenty manat

hosts.Leyla: lives in Baku and loves a good plan
hosts.Sam: grew up in Manchester and once travelled with no plan at all

before.predict: What is the oldest thing you own? Guess: what did Sam buy at the flea market?

lines.t: Hi everyone, and welcome to the SpeakLab Podcast. I'm Leyla.
And I'm Sam. Today's topic is old and second-hand things. And I bought something on Sunday.
Let me guess. Something old?
A record player. Second-hand, from the flea market near the metro. Twenty manat!
Does it work?
Perfectly. It's from the seventies — real vintage. And the seller gave me five old records for free.
[laugh] You and your free gifts at markets. What music?
Azerbaijani jazz! I'd never heard it before. It's beautiful.
I have something old too. I inherited my grandfather's watch.
Doesn't your grandmother want it?
She gave it to me. It's not worth much money, but it's my favourite keepsake.
Old things have stories. New things don't.
Do you remember the samovar in our attic? For twenty years we let it gather dust.
The big copper one?
Yes. Mr Aliyev took it to his garage and restored it. Now it shines like new, and we use it every Sunday.
He can fix anything. That man is an antique himself! [chuckle]
Sam! I'll tell him you said that.
Please don't. Some things really stand the test of time — like his figs.
And your old leather jacket?
Fifteen years old, from a second-hand shop in Manchester. Still my favourite.
Here's your question for your next SpeakLab call: what is the oldest thing you own — and is there a story behind it?
Mine is the jacket. Or maybe now the record player. See you next time!
Bye for now!
